timeline.title: A Short History of Anniversaries
items: In parts of Germany, the story goes, wives wore a silver wreath at 25 years of marriage and a gold one at 50.
Queen Victoria celebrated sixty years on the throne with a Diamond Jubilee. Diamond has meant sixty ever since.
Emily Post's etiquette book listed gifts for the big anniversaries, from paper in year one to gold at fifty.
Jewellers in America grew the list so almost every year had its own present, from paper to diamond.
today: {years} years married. Not in the history books, but the start of our whole family.

letters.title: What the Poets Say About Lasting Love
items: Grow old along with me! The best is yet to be.
How do I love thee? Let me count the ways.
Love does not consist in gazing at each other, but in looking outward together in the same direction.
Antoine de Saint-Exupéry, Wind, Sand and Stars
The heart that loves is always young.
letters.hand: The poets say it beautifully. We just say: here is to you two, {who}.

facts.title: The Science of Lasting Love
items: Some couples married for decades still show the brain activity of new love when they see each other's photo.
Couples who laugh together tend to feel closer and happier in their marriage.
Holding the hand of someone you love can calm the body's stress response.
Swans often stay with the same partner for many years, raising their young together.
Gold is given at fifty years because, like a long marriage, it does not tarnish.
Happy couples share about five kind moments for every grumpy one.
facts.hand: Science can explain a lot. It cannot explain how you two make it look so easy.

note.title: What we believe lasting love is
paras: We make magazines for a living, but some feel different. This was one of them.
We believe lasting love is built from small things: the tea brought without asking, the joke that still works years later, the hand that finds yours at the end of a long day.
{who}, your family wanted you to have something special. Not a card that ends up in a drawer, but pages full of your story, and of everyone it made.
That someone is {from}. And from everything they told us, you are the reason this family is what it is.
